name: Oviedo siege – the old town
story: On 19 July 1936 Colonel Antonio Aranda, who had persuaded Republican leaders he was loyal, declared for the rising and held Oviedo with soldiers, Civil Guards and Falangist volunteers. The city was surrounded by Asturian miners' militias. It survived months of siege, shelling and street fighting, including around the Plaza de la Constitución and the cathedral, until a Nationalist column from Galicia opened a narrow corridor on 16–17 October 1936. The Republican offensive of February 1937, supported by T-26 tanks, failed. The old centre was heavily damaged.
see: The town hall on Plaza de la Constitución, facing San Isidoro church, in an old quarter that was largely rebuilt after siege damage.
plan: Central Oviedo, on foot. Earlier versions of this guide listed a memorial to the defenders inside the town hall; whether it is still on display has not been confirmed.

boxes.text: Casualty figures for the siege vary between sources and are not given here; civilian deaths are unclear.
